root.label: Strings, views, and spans
root.note: Contiguous sequence types divide into heap-capable owners and lightweight non-owning pointer-length descriptors.

children.label: std::string ownership
children.note: Owns a contiguous character buffer uniquely with a guaranteed trailing null terminator.

children.label: Small String Optimization
children.note: Short strings live inline inside the object footprint, avoiding heap allocation.

children.label: Move invalidation
children.note: Moving an SSO string copies inline bytes, leaving prior views pointing at the source.

children.label: Trailing null invariant
children.note: Since C++11, data()[size()] is always CharT(), shared identically by c_str().

children.label: resize_and_overwrite
children.note: C++23 method lets C APIs populate capacity directly without pre-zeroing memory.

children.label: std::string_view borrowing
children.note: Trivially copyable two-word descriptor of read-only characters passed by value.

children.label: Missing null terminator
children.note: Slicing via remove_suffix does not write a null byte, making printf with data() unsafe.

children.label: Dangling lifetimes
children.note: Binding a view to a temporary std::string dangles immediately at the semicolon.

children.label: Deleted nullptr ctor
children.note: C++23 deletes basic_string_view(nullptr_t) to turn null construction into a compile error.

children.label: std::span descriptors
children.note: Non-owning contiguous range wrapper generalizing pointer and count for any element type.

children.label: Static vs dynamic extent
children.note: Static extent span<T, N> stores one pointer, whereas dynamic span<T> stores pointer and count.

children.label: Shallow constness
children.note: const span<T> allows mutating elements; write span<const T> for read-only views.

children.label: Raw byte views
children.note: as_bytes and as_writable_bytes reinterpret contiguous elements as std::byte spans.

children.label: API boundary rules
children.note: Return owning containers upward and pass non-owning views downward by value.

children.label: borrowed_range opt-in
children.note: Both string_view and span satisfy borrowed_range so range algorithms return real iterators.

children.label: Slicing subranges
children.note: Use first, last, and subspan to narrow views in constant time without allocations.
